title: 工学基礎Ⅰ
subtitle: Mathematical Basics for Engineering I
educationalGoal: Students will learn about machinery, electricity/electronics (EE) technology, and information—the three major technologies for manufacturing that support society—as preparation to become “an engineer to consider and act on their own.” In addition, students will be trained to develop the fundamental mathematical skills essential in these fields.
advice: 1. Introduction of academic fields: Students will learn about the academic areas in electrical and electronic engineering and the research efforts in those areas through specific examples. 2. Development of fundamental mathematical skills: Students will review and have training in basic equations and mathematical functions (trigonometric function, exponential function, and logarithmic function) as well as complex numbers (vectors), which will be widely needed in their future studies and work.
books: A textbook written in Japanese will be used.
requiredKnowledge: This course is an introduction to the field of electrical and electronic engineering. It is important to pay close attention to the technology in which each student is interested. It is also important to review mathematics (simultaneous equations, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, etc.) learned in high school for future learning. It is desirable to study areas that were not taken in high school using self-study and learning support systems in our university.

activityGoals.body: To understand the role of the Faculty of Engineering in modern society and to make your own study plan.
To understand the basics of thinking as an engineer and the attitude of learning.
To understand how to solve simultaneous equations using the substitution method, addition and subtraction method
To understand how to calculate basic functions.
To understand how to describe and calculate complex numbers.
